audit_findings.title: The leasing operation may earn profits without charging all required capital
audit_findings.magnitude: $69.8m of 2025 lease-equipment purchases less $18.4m of off-lease sale proceeds = $51.4m; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE includes sales-type leasing operating profit but may omit recurring investment in lease equipment, receivables, and inventory.
audit_findings.evidence: We finance various types of transportation-related equipment for independent third parties under lease contracts which are generally for one to three years and accounted for as sales-type leases with fully guaranteed residual values.
audit_findings.explanation: No omission is yet demonstrated because the $61.5m of lease receipts and changes in lease receivables and inventory must also be traced. However, the $51.4m net equipment outlay equals 54% of the $94.9m OE anchor, so an omitted recurring capital charge could materially reduce operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile leasing revenue, cost of goods sold, lease receipts, equipment purchases and sales, and changes in lease receivables and tractor inventory; then rerun OE with the recurring net investment charged exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year capex may be below sustainable replacement needs
audit_findings.magnitude: $400.0m-$450.0m 2026 forecast versus $289.2m in 2025, a $110.8m-$160.8m increase; replacement portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An understated recurring capital charge inflates the $94.9m OE anchor and every discounted operating cash flow derived from it.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect 2026 net capital expenditures to range from $400.0 - $450.0 million, including $78.2 million of firm purchase commitments disclosed in Note 13, Commitments and Contingencies .
audit_findings.explanation: A replacement-capex shortfall is not demonstrated because the forecast may include growth investment and timing differences. Nevertheless, the forecast increase exceeds the entire OE anchor; if treated as recurring without offsetting growth economics, it would reduce the anchor to between negative $15.9m and negative $65.9m.
audit_findings.action: Separate replacement, growth, land, technology, and facility spending; normalize replacement investment over a full fleet cycle and rerun the valuation if normalized recurring capex differs materially from $289.2m.

audit_findings.title: An uninsured adverse judgment may be an incremental claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured or underaccrued judgment principal and accrued interest would reduce the equity bridge or future OE, after excluding amounts already expensed or accrued.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, in 2025, the limits of our excess insurance coverage were exhausted for one specific policy year as a result of a 2024 adverse verdict in a lawsuit arising out of a fatal motor vehicle accident that a Schneider driver is alleged to have caused, in addition to other losses occurring in that same policy year, with interest continuing to accrue on the judgment.
audit_findings.explanation: The record demonstrates exhausted excess coverage and continuing judgment interest, but it does not demonstrate an omitted liability. Schneider reported $318.3m of total claims accruals at June 30, 2026 and states that appropriate matters are accrued, yet the claim-specific judgment, insurance recovery, and recorded reserve are undisclosed. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a claim-level reconciliation of judgment principal, accrued interest, appeal status, insurance and reinsurance recoveries, collateral, and the recorded claims accrual; rerun only for the uninsured or underaccrued amount not already recognized.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat all cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $327.1m added, equal to $1.83 per share and 18.0% of the $1,814.0m base equity value; required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding operating or restricted liquidity as a non-operating asset overstates the equity bridge dollar for dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital is required principally to ensure we are able to run the business and have sufficient funds to satisfy maturing short-term debt and operational expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire cash and short-term-investment balance, but the record does not demonstrate that the entire balance is distributable. At June 30, 2026 the company also had $117.5m of insurance-related letters of credit and $197.7m of equipment commitments, although those amounts are not automatically cash deductions. The possible adjustment is large enough to affect value materially.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum operating cash using seasonal working capital, claims-payment timing, insurance collateral, debt requirements, and committed purchases; rerun the bridge adding only cash demonstrably exceeding that reserve.

audit_findings.title: Private strategic stakes may be overstated or double-counted
audit_findings.magnitude: $153.7m added, equal to $0.86 per share and 8.5% of the $1,814.0m base equity value; misstatement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Overvalued stakes inflate the equity bridge, while retained investment income or valuation gains could capitalize the same economics in OE and again in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: These investments are accounted for under ASC 321, Investments - Equity Securities, using the measurement alternative.
audit_findings.explanation: The $153.7m bridge addition is demonstrated, but neither overvaluation nor double counting is demonstrated. The principal private equities were carried at $137.3m under the measurement alternative at June 30, 2026, so current realizable value, preferred-right dilution, and liquidity remain uncertain. The amount is sufficiently large relative to base equity value to require resolution.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every bridge component to carrying value and security terms, obtain current financing and impairment evidence, estimate dilution and senior claims, verify the treatment of investment income and valuation changes in OE, and rerun the bridge for supported adjustments.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $1.5m in FY2018 and $0.6m in FY2019; $0 effect on the 2025 anchor under the stated anchor rule
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A could increase historical OE, but the valuation anchors to 2025 OE rather than the historical trend.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2018 $289.9m (99.5% of filed D&A); FY2019 $292.2m (99.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The residuals are only about 0.5% and 0.2% of filed D&A. Even full add-back would leave 2018 and 2019 OE negative at approximately negative $13.3m and negative $123.3m, respectively. It would not cure the unstable series or change the $94.9m latest-actual anchor.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is needed. Classify the residual components only for documentation unless evidence shows an affected amount in the 2025 anchor year.
